(* Standard fact: if [C] has and [U] preserves [J]-limits, then [=(d) ↓ U] has [J]-limits, and the projection [comma_proj2 : =(d) ↓ U ⟶ C] creates them. *)

statement_record.book: If G : A → X preserves all small products (respectively, all equalizers), then for each x the projection Q : (x ↓ G) → A, sending (s : x → Ga) to a, CREATES all small products (respectively, all equalizers). Mac Lane notes the same argument creates ANY limit (Exercise V.6.1).
statement_record.intree: Definition Comma_Complete (HU : PreservesImageLimit) (HC : @Complete C) : @Complete (=(d) ↓ U) := fun J K => comma_limit HC HU K.  — where the constructed apex is `((ttt, vertex_obj[Ldiag]); phi)` with `Ldiag := HC J Gdiag` and the legs are the projected C-legs.
statement_record.strength_comparison: mixed. intree-stronger in shape coverage: it directly realises Mac Lane's Exercise V.6.1 generalisation — ALL limit shapes at once, not just products and equalizers, and the proof is his (build the C-limit, transport the d-legs through the preserved image cone to a mediating φ, pair up). intree-weaker in two respects: (a) GRANULARITY — both hypotheses quantify over every diagram shape (`HC : @Complete C` and `HU : PreservesImageLimit`, itself a ∀ J G L N statement), so Mac Lane's per-shape implications ('G preserves small products ⇒ Q creates small products'; 'G preserves equalizers ⇒ Q creates equalizers') cannot be recovered by instantiation — there is no way in-tree to conclude anything about the comma category from product-preservation alone; (b) CREATION — what is proven is a construction of the comma limit over the CHOSEN base limit `HC J Gdiag`, not the creation property proper. The hypothesis on U is the cone-level `PreservesImageLimit` rather than the library's apex-only `PreservesLimit`, a documented and correct strengthening (Construction/Comma/Limit.v:47-66) that is inhabited by every right adjoint.

gap: Two precise gaps. (1) No per-shape statement: `Comma_Complete` consumes all-shapes completeness of C and all-shapes image-limit preservation by U, so 'U preserves products ⇒ the comma has products' and 'U preserves equalizers ⇒ the comma has equalizers' — the two clauses Mac Lane actually needs, and the only ones his proof of Theorem 2 uses — are not derivable from what is in-tree. (2) 'Creates' is claimed in the header comment (Construction/Comma/Limit.v:32-33 and Construction/Comma.v:99-100) but not stated as a theorem: the file constructs a limit lying over the chosen base limit, whereas creation additionally asserts that for ANY limit cone of comma_proj2 ○ K in C there is a UNIQUE cone in [=(d) ↓ U] lying over it and that this cone is a limit. statement_record.strength_comparison: same content ONLY after an unrecorded instantiation and translation. `SolutionSet K (terminal_obj Sets)` reads: a Type of indices, objects sol_obj i of D, GLOBAL POINTS sol_arr i : 1 ~{Sets}~> K (sol_obj i), and for every global point h : 1 ~> K c an index i and t : sol_obj i ~> c with fmap[K] t ∘ sol_arr i ≈ h. That is Mac Lane's def3 with 'element of the setoid K a' replaced by 'morphism from the terminal setoid into K a'. The two are equivalent in Sets, but the library records no such bridge, and the element-wise phrasing (∀ d, ∀ x ∈ K d, ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ y ∈ K s, ∃ f, K f y = x) appears nowhere. As with def2, `sol_covers` is a Type-valued choice rather than an existence, and 'small set S' is `sol_index : Type` with size carried by universe polymorphism.

evidence.intree_statement: Record OpSignature := { operation : Type ; (* (Names of) operations. *) arity : operation → Type (* Each operation has an arity. *) }.
Record OpAlgebra (S : OpSignature) := { carrier :> Type ; op : ∀ o : operation S, (arity o → carrier) → carrier (* no equations *) }.

Record EqSignature (S : OpSignature) := { eq :> Type ; eq_arity : eq → Type ; lhs : ∀ (A : OpAlgebra S) (e : eq), (eq_arity e → A) → A ; rhs : ∀ (A : OpAlgebra S) (e : eq), (eq_arity e → A) → A ; lhs_natural : ∀ A B (f : AlgHom A B) e args, f (lhs A e args) = lhs B e (fun i => f (args i)) ; rhs_natural : ... }.
Record Algebra (S : OpSignature) (E : EqSignature S) := { alg :> OpAlgebra S ; equations : ∀ (e : E) (args : eq_arity e → alg), lhs e args = rhs e args }.

Inductive nullary : Set := . Inductive unary : Set := Only. Inductive binary : Set := Fst | Snd. Inductive ternary : Set := One | Two | Three.  (* the finite arities Mac Lane names: arity 2 = binary, arity 3 = ternary *)
Definition Signature : Type := nat -> nat -> Type.  (* the nat-graded variant: [Sig m n] is the Type of generator names with m input wires (the domain/arity) and n output wires *)
Record SMT : Type := { smt_sig : Signature; smt_eqs : EqSystem smt_sig }.  (* 'A symmetric monoidal theory: generators plus equations' — the (Ω, E) pair *)

statement_record.book: A type τ of an algebraic system consists of a set Ω of operators together with a set E of identities. Ω is a GRADED SET: a set with a function assigning to each ω ∈ Ω a natural number n, its arity (arity 2 = binary, 3 = ternary, ...). An ACTION A of Ω on a set S assigns to each operator ω of arity n an n-ary operation ω_A : S^n → S, where S^n is the n-fold cartesian product.
statement_record.intree: Record OpSignature := { operation : Type ; arity : operation → Type }.  Record OpAlgebra (S : OpSignature) := { carrier :> Type ; op : ∀ o : operation S, (arity o → carrier) → carrier }.  Record EqSignature (S : OpSignature) := { eq :> Type ; eq_arity : eq → Type ; lhs, rhs : ∀ (A : OpAlgebra S) (e : eq), (eq_arity e → A) → A ; lhs_natural ; rhs_natural }.  Record Algebra (S : OpSignature) (E : EqSignature S) := { alg :> OpAlgebra S ; equations : ∀ e args, lhs e args = rhs e args }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger, with two presentational deviations. STRONGER: `arity : operation → Type` grades by an arbitrary TYPE rather than by a natural number, so infinitary operations are admitted (the file says so explicitly: 'The main trick is that the arity of an operation is *not* a number but rather a type. For instance, the arity of a binary operation is a type with two elements. (And nothing prevents us from having an infinite type as arity.)'); Mac Lane's finite case is recovered by the supplied `nullary/unary/binary/ternary` arities, and the nat-graded reading is available separately as `Signature : nat -> nat -> Type` (Construction/PROP/Signature.v:50, itself bigraded so a generator may have any output coarity, a further generalisation of Mac Lane's single-output operators). DEVIATIONS, both recorded rather than hidden: (1) the n-ary operation S^n → S is written in exponential form `(arity o → carrier) → carrier` rather than as an n-fold cartesian product — isomorphic, and the standard dependently-typed encoding; (2) `carrier :> Type` is a bare Type with Leibniz `=`, not one of the library's hom-setoids, and `AlgHom.op_commute` / `Algebra.equations` are stated with `=` — a deliberate departure from the library's setoid discipline confined to this Coq-native instance file (which also costs it functional extensionality at Instance/Comp.v:130). `EqSignature` moreover REQUIRES lhs/rhs to be natural in the algebra, a well-formedness condition Mac Lane leaves implicit ('This way it's impossible to write down strange equations that involve something other than the operations') — i.e. it forces the two sides of an identity to be derived operators, which is exactly his intent.

verifier.notes: I OVERTURN MY OWN preliminary here, in the classifier's favour. My blind pass started from the PROP spine (Construction/PROP/Signature.v's Signature : nat -> nat -> Type and Presentation.v's SMT) and was heading for PARTIAL on the grounds that a PROP generator is many-in/many-out and its valuations land in an arbitrary PROP rather than acting on a SET. The classifier found the better counterpart, which I then read in full: Instance/Comp.v's universal-algebra module is a direct match for Mac Lane's τ = (Ω, E). Verified at the cited lines — OpSignature (:45) is the graded set of operators (operation : Type, arity : operation → Type); OpAlgebra (:54) is exactly an ACTION of Ω on a carrier, op : ∀ o, (arity o → carrier) → carrier, i.e. ω_A : S^n → S in exponential form; EqSignature (:240) is the set E of identities with lhs/rhs plus naturality; Algebra S E (:268) is the algebraic system of type τ; and nullary/unary/binary/ternary (:274-277) supply Mac Lane's named finite arities. The strength_comparison is honest about all three deviations (Type-graded rather than nat-graded arity, exponential rather than cartesian-power form, and the Leibniz-equality/bare-Type departure from the library's setoid discipline that costs functional extensionality at :130). Instance/Comp.v is _CoqProject-registered (line 177) with a .vo present. PRESENT is right.

evidence.intree_statement: Inductive Tree : Type := | generator : X → Tree | node : ∀ (o : operation S), (arity o → Tree) → Tree.  Definition Free : OpAlgebra S := {| carrier := Tree; op := node |}.  (* Mac Lane's composition clause ω(λ₁,...,λₙ) is `node` *)

Fixpoint induced_map (t : Tree) : A := match t with | generator x => h x | node o arg => op A o (fun i => induced_map (arg i)) end.  (* h : X → A; taking A := Free S Y and h := fun i => generator (f i) is substitution along an arbitrary f : X → Y *)
Definition induced_hom : AlgHom Free A.  (* existence half: every action A of S on a set, plus a valuation h of the variables, extends to a homomorphism out of the term algebra *)
Theorem from_free_unique (f g : AlgHom Free A) : (∀ x : X, f (generator x) = g (generator x)) → f ≈ g.  (* uniqueness half of 'every action of Ω extends uniquely' *)

Inductive Term : nat -> nat -> Type := | T_id : forall n, Term n n | T_braid : forall m n, Term (m + n) (n + m) | T_comp : forall {m n p}, Term n p -> Term m n -> Term m p | T_tens : forall {m1 n1 m2 n2}, Term m1 n1 -> Term m2 n2 -> Term (m1 + m2) (n1 + n2) | T_gen : forall {m n}, S m n -> Term m n.  (* the ARITY-GRADED derived-operator candidate — but the only variable-rearranging generator is the braid *)

Theorem interp_unique : ∀ m n (t : Term S m n), ...  (* any strict symmetric competitor agreeing with the valuation v on generators agrees on all terms — the unique-extension property at the arity-graded level *)

statement_record.book: From Ω one forms the set Λ of all DERIVED OPERATORS, closed under: (composition) given ω of arity n and derived λ₁,...,λₙ of arities m₁,...,mₙ, the composite ω(λ₁,...,λₙ) is derived of arity m₁+...+mₙ; (substitution) given λ of arity n and ANY function f : n → m between finite sets, substitution of f into λ yields a derived operator θ of arity m with θ(x₁,...,x_m) = λ(x_{f1},...,x_{fn}). Every action A of Ω on a set S extends uniquely to an action of Λ on S.
statement_record.intree: Inductive Tree := generator : X → Tree | node : ∀ o, (arity o → Tree) → Tree;  Definition Free := {| carrier := Tree; op := node |};  Definition induced_hom : AlgHom Free A;  Theorem from_free_unique (f g : AlgHom Free A) : (∀ x : X, f (generator x) = g (generator x)) → f ≈ g.  Separately, arity-graded: Inductive Term : nat -> nat -> Type (T_id / T_braid / T_comp / T_tens / T_gen) with Theorem interp_unique.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in packaging and, for the graded version, in the substitution clause. The Comp.v term algebra realises Mac Lane's clauses in substance — composition is `node`, substitution along an arbitrary f (including duplication and deletion of variables) is `induced_map` at A := Free S Y with h := generator ∘ f, and the unique-extension claim is `induced_hom` + `from_free_unique` — but `Tree` is a single unindexed type, never presented as an arity-GRADED set Λ, and no 'action of Λ on S' is ever packaged as a structure. The arity-graded in-tree candidate, `Term S m n`, is strictly the SYMMETRIC MONOIDAL (linear) closure: its only variable-rearranging generator is `T_braid`, a bijection, so substitution along a non-injective or non-surjective f : n → m is not expressible — the cartesian closure Mac Lane means is not what `Term` computes. `from_free_unique` also costs functional extensionality (Instance/Comp.v:124-130, flagged in-file: 'How to remove this axiom? ... genuinely needs functional extensionality').

gap: Three precise gaps. (1) The arity-graded set Λ of derived operators is never defined: `Instance/Comp.v`'s `Tree` is unindexed (an element is a term over a whole variable type X, not an operator of a specific arity n), and no operation on it is named as 'composition' or 'substitution' — both are available only by instantiating `induced_map`. (2) No 'action of Λ on S' is packaged, so 'every action of Ω extends uniquely to an action of Λ' exists only in its free-algebra guise (`induced_hom` + `from_free_unique`), never in the form of the book's statement. (3) The only arity-graded term development in the tree, `Construction/PROP/Term.v`'s `Term S m n`, closes under composition, tensor and BRAIDS only, so Mac Lane's substitution clause along an arbitrary f : n → m (duplication/deletion of variables) is not available there; the cartesian counterpart — a free Lawvere theory or free cartesian PROP on a signature, whose hom n → 1 would BE Λ_n — is not constructed: `Theory/Lawvere.v:116` `LawvereTheory` is a class over an abstract cartesian category, and the only in-tree instance `FinSetOp_Lawvere` (Instance/FinSet/Lawvere.v) is the base theory on FinSet^op with no generating operations.
